# Code review: unify Safe list sorting (WA-2567)

**How this ran:** I did it as a single-reviewer draft, not the full pipeline. There were no separate validator/refuter agents and no category sub-agents, so the findings are unconfirmed and there is **no score**. I didn't modify any files, run tests or use `gh`.

**Scope:** 16 files, +338 −25. Base `d65b681` (the merge-base of `7d1ccd5`) → `HEAD 8ba399c` (2 commits). Everything is in `apps/web`. Onchain code, `packages/` and mobile are untouched.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **Open the PR after deciding on #1.** Nothing blocks merge. |
| Main concern | The one-time migration to A→Z only overrides people who deliberately picked a sort order. Everyone else already gets the new default without it. |
| Fix first | #1, then the placeholder copy (#3) |

## Findings

### 1. The one-time reset wipes deliberate choices, and doesn't stick until the user changes sort again · regression · P2
`apps/web/src/store/index.ts:146-154` (also the comment at `apps/web/src/store/orderByPreferenceSlice.ts:10-11`)

- **What happens:**
  - The `orderByPreference` value is only saved to localStorage when an action whose name starts with `orderByPreference/` runs (`persistState` in `store/persistStore.ts`).
  - Before this change, the only thing that dispatched `setOrderByPreference` was the explicit sort control in `AccountListFilters`.
  - So users who stayed on the old default have **nothing saved**. They already get `NAME` from the new `initialState`, and the reset does nothing for them.
  - The reset only changes anything for users who **explicitly chose "Most recent"**. It flips them to Name.
  - `@@HYDRATE` isn't a slice action, so `resetVersion` is never saved on hydrate. The reset runs again on every load until the user changes the sort themselves.
- **Why it matters:** The comment says it "resets users still on the previous default". In practice it does the opposite: it discards an explicit preference, and the saved state never records that the migration ran.
- **The guard doesn't do what it says:** after `merge({}, state, payload)` the slice is always present, so the `orderByState &&` check is always true. The "only touches a real store" comment is misleading.
- **Fix:** drop the reset. The `initialState` change alone moves everyone who never chose to A→Z. If product really wants to override explicit choices, say so in the comment, and accept that the flag isn't saved until the next sort change.
- **Tests:** `store/__tests__/index.test.ts:149` currently locks in the override behaviour. Update it together with the fix.

### 2. Space safe names use exact-case address-book lookups · bugs · P3
`apps/web/src/features/spaces/hooks/useSpaceSafes.tsx:31-34`, which feeds `hooks/safes/useAllSafesGrouped.ts:58`

- **What happens:**
  - `lodash/merge` combines the local address book with the space contacts, keeping each address key exactly as stored.
  - `_buildSafeItems` then looks names up with `allSafeNames[chainId]?.[address]`, an exact-case match.
  - The existing `useSafeNameResolver` (`hooks/useAllAddressBooks.ts:188-198`) lowercases keys for exactly this reason.
- **Effect:**
  - If a local entry and the CGW space-safe address differ in casing, the item gets no `name` and sorts last under "Name", while the row still shows the address-book name.
  - Two differently cased keys for the same address can also let a local name win over the space contact.
- **Fix:** build the name source with lowercased keys, or reuse the resolver's lowercase map.
- **Confidence:** moderate. The same exact-case lookup already exists in the non-space `useAllSafes` path.

### 3. Search placeholder is a lowercase fragment with no verb · conventions · P3
`apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SafeSelectorDropdown/components/SafeDropdownContainer.tsx:154`

- The placeholder is now `"by name, address or network"`.
- This breaks the root AGENTS.md sentence-case rule for UI text.
- It's inconsistent with the sibling modal, which says `"Search by name or address"` (`AccountsModal/index.tsx:133`).
- The input has no `aria-label`, so this fragment is also the field's only accessible name.
- **Fix:** use `"Search by name, address or network"`, or a shorter version that keeps "Search".

### 4. New `SafeListSortToggle` component has no Storybook story · conventions · P3
`apps/web/src/components/common/SafeListSortToggle/index.tsx:24`

`apps/web/AGENTS.md:10` and `:160` require a story for a new component with logic. Only `index.test.tsx` was added.

### 5. The toggle's dispatch is untested · testing · P3
`apps/web/src/components/common/SafeListSortToggle/index.test.tsx:8`

- The only test checks the default trigger label.
- If the `onValueChange` → `setOrderByPreference` wiring (including the unchecked `value as OrderByOption` cast) were deleted or broken, no test would fail.
- The test's comment says base-ui menus don't open in jsdom. The repo already works around that by mocking `@/components/ui/dropdown-menu` elsewhere, so the same approach would let a test fire a selection and check the store.

### 6. Space-context ordering isn't covered · testing · P3
`apps/web/src/components/common/SpaceSafeBar/hooks/useSafeBarSafes.ts:99-104`, tests at `hooks/__tests__/useSafeBarSafes.test.ts:99-122`

- `spaceDropdownSafes` is new behaviour: it pins the current safe first and re-sorts the rest.
- The space-context tests each use a single safe, and the new sorting tests (`:332`, `:346`) only cover non-space.
- Nothing would catch a regression in space ordering or in the current-safe pinning there.

## Not sure about this one
- **Stale current safe on space routes:** `safeAddress` falls back to the Redux `safeInfo`. On a space route that value can still hold a safe from outside the space, and `spaceDropdownSafes` would then put that safe at the top of the list (`useSafeBarSafes.ts:99-104`). Before this change the space list was passed through untouched. A single-chain safe is probably hidden by the `selectedItemId` filter in `SafeDropdownContainer.tsx:84`, but I couldn't prove that for the multi-chain or stale case.
- **Toggle nested in the Select popup:** `SafeListSortToggle` is a `DropdownMenu` inside a base-ui `Select` popup. Whether clicking it closes the parent Select can only be checked in a browser. The container test replaces it with a stub.

## Checked, nothing found
- **Security:** nothing new crosses a trust boundary. Local address-book names stay on the client.
- **Performance:** the comparators are stable, module-level functions. The merge is memoised. `safeItems` in `useSpaceSafes` isn't memoised, but it wasn't before this change either.
- **Correctness of `lastVisited`:** the new `_buildSafeItems` code reads `lastVisited` the same way `useAllSafes.ts:60` does.

## Worth tidying (optional)
- Replace the merge-and-lookup in `useSpaceSafes` with the existing lowercase-keyed name resolution in `useAllAddressBooks.ts`. That fixes #2 as well.
